# Quantum biology and cellular computation — synthesis note

**Status:** speculation grounded in a literature scan, not a project deliverable.
**Date:** 2026-05-01
**Author context:** Generated by Claude during a conversation with Naresh exploring whether the Dark Manifold concept's "cellular quantum computation" framing has support in published work.

## Scope

This document is the deeper version of "do quantum biology and the cellular quantum coprocessor idea have empirical support, and what theory does the actual evidence allow." It exists in the repo because the conversation that generated it was load-bearing for thinking about Dark Manifold next steps; it is not a phase, not a fact, and not part of the cell_sim production stack. The production simulator (cell_sim/, regulation YAML, v15/v16 baselines) is unchanged.

It is NOT a peer-reviewed assessment, NOT based on full paper reads (WebFetch was blocked at the proxy across all bio databases; this synthesis rests on WebSearch snippets and my training-data knowledge of the field through early 2026). Take it as a snapshot of where I think the published evidence sits, calibrated against my best honest read.

## Method

- 8 targeted WebSearches against arXiv, bioRxiv, PMC, Nature, RSC Publishing, Frontiers, ACS, PubMed.
- Coverage: photosynthesis (FMO + LH2), cryptochrome magnetoreception, enzyme tunneling (Klinman/Schwartz), Penrose-Hameroff Orch OR, decoherence in warm wet systems, McKemmish/Reimers critique, Levin bioelectric / non-neural cognition, tryptophan superradiance, vibrational theory of olfaction.
- Where snippets gave direct quotes from abstracts or summaries, I extracted them.
- WebFetch returned 403 from every URL tried, so I could not read full papers. Quantitative claims below come from search-result summaries; treat them as paraphrase, not direct quotation.

## Evidence map

| Claim | Status | Evidence | Counter-evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hydrogen / proton tunneling is widespread in enzyme catalysis | **Robust** | Klinman / Schwartz programs spanning 30+ years; soybean lipoxygenase-1 kH/kD ≈ 80 (one of the largest KIEs ever measured); Chemical Reviews 2006/2014 reviews; widespread KIE measurements across enzyme classes | None substantive. Mechanism well-characterized. |
| Cryptochrome radical-pair mechanism enables avian magnetoreception | **Robust and growing** | Schulten radical-pair theory (2000); ErCry4 magnetic sensitivity in vitro (Nature 2021); ErCry4a lipid-bilayer ordering (ACS Chem Biol 2024); quantum Zeno effect involvement (Nat Commun 2024); flavin–tryptophan radical pair pathways characterized | One bioRxiv preprint (Feb 2025) suggests Cry4b may not be the radical-pair magnetoreceptor in the European robin specifically; doesn't refute the mechanism, refutes one candidate protein |
| Long-lived (~ps) electronic coherence drives photosynthetic energy-transfer efficiency | **Substantially walked back** | Original Engel/Fleming 2007 2D spectroscopy claim; PNAS 2010 "long-lived coherence at physiological temperature" | Recent re-analysis (Duan et al., others) shows electronic coherence lifetime is ~60 fs at room temperature; long-lived oscillations originally interpreted as electronic coherence are now identified as **vibrational or vibronic ground-state modes** unrelated to energy transfer. Science Advances 2020 paper title: "Do photosynthetic complexes use quantum coherence to increase their efficiency? **Probably not**" |
| Penrose-Hameroff Orch OR (microtubule consciousness via Fröhlich condensation) | **Strongly contested** | Hameroff lab continues to publish supportive interpretations; recent (2024) tryptophan-superradiance paper (Babcock et al., J. Phys. Chem. B); 2024-2025 work on anesthetic binding to tubulin aromatic rings, claimed disruption of a 613 THz mode | Reimers, McKemmish, McKenzie, Mark, Hush (2009/2013) — the Fröhlich condensation Orch OR requires would need temperatures >500 K to be biologically significant; "untenable in a biological environment" |
| Tryptophan superradiance in microtubule networks (Babcock et al. 2024) | **Theoretical w/ partial experimental support** | Cooperative emission predicted from networks of >10⁵ tryptophan UV transition dipoles; fluorescence quantum-yield enhancement experimentally observed for hierarchically-organized tubulin | The phenomenon is real for collective optical response; the leap to "this enables cellular cognition or computation" is not made by the data — that's interpretation contributed by Hameroff and the consciousness community |
| Vibrational theory of olfaction (Turin) | **Contested** | Drosophila distinguishing isotopologues of odorants; Wright/Turin theory; some replication | Failures to replicate in mammals; lock-and-key shape model is the alternative; "swipe card" hybrid models proposed |
| Cellular quantum coprocessor as unifying explanation for cellular computation | **Speculation** | None direct. The strongest individual quantum-biology cases (enzyme tunneling, cryptochrome) don't compose into a unified network claim. | The well-supported quantum effects are **local, isolated, and bespoke** — none of them are network phenomena; none cross-couple to other cellular subsystems; none provide a substrate for distributed quantum computation |
| Cells perform meaningful computation at all (cellular cognition / non-neural intelligence) | **Robust** — but classical | Levin lab's bioelectric work (Communications Biology 2024, BioEssays 2025); ion channels + gap junctions as voltage-gated current conductances forming "transistors with historicity"; aneural cells perform basic logic operations; somatic bioelectric signaling is a real cellular computation substrate | The cellular computation Levin describes is **entirely classical bioelectric**, not quantum. This is important for the synthesis. |

## What the evidence supports — the modest theory

I'll call this the **Local Quantum Tools** view:

> Cells exploit quantum effects opportunistically, at specific localized sites, for specific functions where classical mechanisms are inadequate. Each instance is bespoke. There is no general "cellular quantum coprocessor"; there are isolated quantum **tools** embedded in a fundamentally classical biological substrate.

Specifically:

- **Enzyme active sites** use proton / hydrogen / electron tunneling because tunneling is faster than thermal activation for the relevant barriers. The quantum effect is local (single active site), short-lived (picoseconds), and doesn't network with other quantum effects elsewhere in the cell.
- **Cryptochrome** uses radical-pair spin coherence because it is the only known mechanism by which a small biological molecule can detect Earth-strength magnetic fields. The coherence is local (one protein), microsecond-scale, and doesn't propagate.
- **Photosynthetic energy transfer** is fundamentally quantum-mechanical (it's exciton transfer, period) but the *long-lived electronic coherence as efficiency mechanism* claim has been substantially walked back. The actual transfer is well-explained by vibrationally-assisted incoherent hopping with some vibronic mixing — quantum mechanics in the trivial sense, not quantum computation.

This view explains the strong evidence pieces, accommodates the FMO retraction, doesn't need Fröhlich condensates, and is consistent with the Levin classical-bioelectric picture of cellular computation. It is also the view most working quantum biologists would agree with as of 2025-2026.

## What the evidence does NOT support — the strong theory

The "cellular quantum coprocessor" version of the dream — cells maintain a small set of quantum-coherent subsystems that handle the actual decision-making computation, with the classical bulk doing bookkeeping — has **no direct empirical support** in the published literature. Specifically, no published work demonstrates:

- Cross-coupling of quantum coherent subsystems (e.g., two enzymes' active-site quantum events becoming correlated such that information flows between them quantum-mechanically)
- Cellular decisions whose outcome depends on multi-subsystem coherence
- Information-theoretic measures of cellular state showing structure that classical models cannot account for
- Cellular computational efficiency measurably below any classical lower bound for the same task
- Active cellular machinery to protect coherence beyond the few well-characterized cases (FMO, cryptochrome)

The Penrose-Hameroff Orch OR program is the closest to a published unified theory of cellular quantum computation, and it remains **contested at the foundation**: McKemmish / Reimers / McKenzie / Mark / Hush showed in 2009 and 2013 that the Fröhlich condensation Orch OR requires would need temperatures inconsistent with biology. The 2024 tryptophan-superradiance work (Babcock et al.) demonstrates a genuine collective-optical effect in microtubule networks, but the leap from "tubulin tryptophans cooperatively emit UV photons" to "this is the substrate of consciousness or cellular cognition" is interpretation, not data. The consciousness inference is contributed by the Hameroff lab and allied researchers; the underlying optics paper does not make it.

## What this means for the conversation about whole-cell simulation

The dream version we discussed earlier — "cells compute cheaply because they exploit quantum effects we don't model, so the 10¹² compute gap to whole-cell MD is illusory" — does not survive a literature scan. The published evidence allows that quantum tools enable a few specific cellular functions (catalysis acceleration, magnetoreception, possibly olfaction), but does not allow that cellular computation in general routes through quantum channels at network scale.

Concrete implications for the cell simulator project:

1. **The compute gap is not illusory.** The 10¹² FLOP gap between sandbox compute and atom-level whole-cell MD is real. There is no published evidence that cells do *not* pay the classical compute cost of their dynamics — they pay it by being made of physics, but the physics is overwhelmingly classical at the cellular-decision scale.
2. **The right cellular computation model is classical bioelectric + classical chemistry + a handful of quantum tools localized to specific machines.** This is exactly what cell_sim is, with one extension: the quantum tools (catalysis tunneling, cryptochrome spin coherence) are absorbed into effective rate constants and Michaelis-Menten kinetics, which is the right level of abstraction given that none of them networks.
3. **Levin's bioelectric framework is more relevant to "cells as computers" than any quantum framework.** It's classical, well-evidenced, and operates at the cellular timescale. If the project wants a "cells as computational systems" inductive bias, this is where the published evidence points.
4. **Dark Manifold's "quantum + dark matter coupling + superposition collapse" framing is not refuted by this scan but is also not supported.** The pieces of quantum biology that are well-supported don't compose into the Dark Manifold's unified picture. The unbuilt parts of Dark Manifold remain unbuilt and the published evidence neither confirms nor denies them.

## Where the field is going

A few directions visible in 2024-2026 publications:

- **Quantum sensing for biology** — using quantum sensors (NV centers in diamond, atomic magnetometers) to *detect* biological signals at higher sensitivity. Not the same as biology being quantum; it's measurement infrastructure.
- **Quantum algorithms for biology** — running classical biology problems (metabolic pathway analysis, protein folding) on quantum hardware. The bioRxiv 2025 "Quantum Algorithm for Metabolic Network Analysis" paper is an example. Doesn't require biology to be quantum; treats biology as a hard classical problem amenable to quantum compute.
- **Continued chip-away on Orch OR** — more anesthesia experiments, more superradiance characterization. Most working scientists outside the Hameroff-allied community still treat Orch OR as fringe; the recent supportive papers haven't shifted that consensus.
- **Cryptochrome mechanism refinement** — quantum Zeno effect, Landau-Zener-Stückelberg-Majorana transitions, role of lipid bilayer ordering. The radical-pair mechanism is being refined, not overturned.

The field's center of mass over the next 5-10 years will probably be: enzyme tunneling and cryptochrome treated as solid; photosynthesis treated as quantum-but-not-the-way-the-2007-papers-claimed; everything else treated as either contested or speculative. The "cellular quantum computation" unified picture is unlikely to gain ground without a concrete experimentally-testable proposal, which Orch OR's contested status illustrates is hard to construct.

## Honest limits of this synthesis

- **No full paper reads.** WebFetch was 403'd at every URL tried. The synthesis rests on WebSearch result snippets and my training-data knowledge through early 2026. Specific quantitative claims (e.g., kH/kD ≈ 80, electronic-coherence lifetime ~60 fs) come from search-result summaries; for a real paper-grade synthesis these would need verification.
- **Selection bias.** I ran 8 searches based on terms I picked. A different search strategy would surface different evidence.
- **Author selection.** Some prominent quantum-biology researchers (Anthony Marais, Jim Al-Khalili, Johnjoe McFadden) didn't surface in my queries but have published reviews; their views might shift the synthesis.
- **My training cutoff.** Anything published after January 2026 isn't represented.
- **No new claims here.** This document doesn't introduce a new theory; it positions the existing claims against the existing evidence and notes which combination of claims survives.

## What I'd recommend if you wanted to push further

If the project wanted to invest more in quantum-biology-aware modeling for the cell simulator, the highest-value bets would be:

1. **Make the quantum tools explicit in cell_sim.** Currently the simulator absorbs enzyme tunneling into kcat values (which is correct). A version that exposes tunneling-rate temperature dependence, isotope effects, and cryptochrome-style spin dynamics as separately-tunable parameters would let you ask "does the simulator's predictive accuracy improve if quantum tools are modeled explicitly?" The honest expected answer is "no, because the kcat absorption is sufficient at cellular timescales" — but the test is informative.
2. **Use Levin-style bioelectric primitives as a Dark-Manifold-shaped layer.** This is a real, classical, well-evidenced framework for cellular computation that maps onto the kind of architectural inductive biases the salvage tests showed work (P11 local field evolution, P13 structural unitarity). A bioelectric-shaped layer in cell_sim is session-sized and has working publication precedent.
3. **Keep Orch OR / cellular quantum coprocessor as a dream, not a build target.** The published evidence does not support investment of project compute or developer time on this direction. Watch the literature; revisit if a concrete experimentally-testable proposal lands.
